newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prosecutor wants 12 years for Palestinian hijacker. [CORRECTED 18:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Prosecutor wants 12 years for Palestinian hijacker. [CORRECTED 18:50 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects throughout to make clear verdict not yet announced)

The prosecutor in the trial of a Palestinian hijacker who seized a Lufthansa jet in 1977 and killed the pilot to back demands by German guerrillas asked a Hamburg court on Tuesday to jail her for 12 years.

Souhaila Andrawes, 42, the last survivor of four hijackers, is charged with the murder of captain Juergen Schumann who was shot at Mogadishu airport in Somalia. She is also charged with hijacking, kidnapping, hostage-taking and attempted murder.

Andrawes had been convicted in Somalia for the hijacking and sentenced to 20 years in jail, but was released after a year and went home to Beirut. She moved to Norway in 1991 and was extradited to Germany four years later.
The hijackers were backing demands by German Red Army Faction guerrillas for the release of 11 of its members from jail.
Prosecutor Volker Homann, summing up, said the four hijackers had decided together to shoot captain Schumann and Andrawes was held responsible though she did not pull the trigger herself.
Andrawes had admitted taking part in the hijack, but denied any responsibility for the captain's murder.
The defence sums up next week and a verdict is expected in the trial the following week. Reuters earlier erroneously reported that Andrawes had been jailed for 12 years.
The hostage drama ended after five days when German GSG-9 commandos stormed the aircraft at Mogadishu airport, killing three of the hijackers and freeing 86 passengers.
Homann said the court should take into account time Andrawes had spent in prison in Mogadishu and Norway.
